agent_assessment: All 7 phases of the plan have landing code in the working tree. The diff-summary reports 0 changed files because the execution agent ran without sandbox mode; changes were applied directly, so I verified by reading files and running targeted builds/tests. DM api + cli + ui + S2D + LPBS all build clean; focused tests (deployment-manager/deployments, /releases, /profiles, /cli/releases, landing-page-business-suite deploy-readiness, scenario-to-desktop pipeline/deploy, DM UI components) all pass. Schema, routes, handlers, CLI subcommands, UI cards, and skill rewrite match the plan's target end state. Two deviations worth noting: (1) the advisory lock uses pg_try_advisory_lock + hashtextextended() + explicit unlock instead of the plan's pg_try_advisory_xact_lock + hashtext() design (semantically equivalent because the handler defer-calls release(), but different from D10=B), and (2) no scenario-to-desktop tests explicitly assert passthrough of ReleaseID/Channel/variant_key through PublishPipelineRequest to lpbs_client.go, which Phase 5 of the plan required. Concurrency-lock test uses a mock repo returning false rather than a real Postgres race; functional coverage is adequate but the live-Postgres concurrency guarantee is not exercised in CI. Overall this is a solid, broad implementation that matches the plan's intent.

evidence.title: Advisory lock deviates from plan D10=B but still profile-scoped
evidence.description: Plan D10=B specified pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('release:' || profile_id)). Implementation at api/releases/repo.go:256-283 uses pg_try_advisory_lock(hashtextextended('release:' || profile_id, 0)) on a dedicated connection, with explicit pg_advisory_unlock + conn.Close in the returned release() func. Handler at releases/handlers.go:262 uses defer release() so the lock is released on every return path. Semantic difference: xact_lock would auto-release on transaction rollback, whereas non-xact needs the defer to fire. Handler does not wrap the orchestration in an explicit tx, so the xact semantics would not have applied anyway. Functionally safe; plan intent (profile-scoped serialization surviving multi-node deploys) is preserved.

improvement_suggestions.description: Add a table-driven test under scenarios/scenario-to-desktop/api/deploy/lpbs_client_test.go (or pipeline/stage_deploy_test.go) that constructs a PublishRequest with ReleaseID='rel-test' and Channel='beta', invokes the LPBS client against an httptest fake, and asserts the outbound commit payload has release_id='rel-test' and the apply payload has variant_key='beta'. This satisfies Phase 5's explicit test requirement and would fail fast if someone drops the plumbing. Also add the inverse case for Channel='stable' → variant_key='default'.

Add a real-Postgres integration test (guarded by testcontainers, in the same package as orchestrator_release_test.go) that opens two DB connections, has one acquire the profile advisory lock via AcquireProfileLock, then attempts a second AcquireProfileLock on the same profile ID and asserts it returns acquired=false. Release and retry to assert the lock drops cleanly. The current mock-based coverage does not exercise the pg_try_advisory_lock call path.

Add a DM→S2D integration test using httptest.NewServer as a fake scenario-to-desktop and set DESKTOP_PACKAGER_URL to point at it. Drive a release via the orchestrator with a populated LPBS release config and assert the inbound PublishPipelineRequest JSON carries all five coords: AppKey, RemoteProfile, Channel, ReleaseID, UpdateURL. Closes the last end-to-end contract gap between DM and S2D.
